Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Health GHS warns of meningitis, dehydration risks as El Niño threatens Ghana during harmattan Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 18 November 2026 5:26pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has warned Ghanaians about potential health risks associated with the anticipated effects of the El Niño weather phenomenon, cautioning that rising temperatures, prolonged dry spells and increased dust levels could heighten vulnerability to meningitis and other climate-related illnesses.
The warning comes as the country enters the harmattan season, with the Ghana Meteorological Agency forecasting El Niño conditions that could bring unusually high temperatures and challenging weather patterns.
In a public health alert issued on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, the Ministry of Health, through the GHS, said the anticipated weather conditions could have significant implications for public health, including increased cases of heat exhaustion, dehydration and respiratory infections.
The Service also identified meningitis as one of the major health concerns, noting that the combination of hot, dry and dusty conditions could increase vulnerability to infections and meningitis outbreaks.
It further warned of prolonged dry spells, rising dust levels and sudden rainfall, with possible flooding in parts of southern Ghana, urging the public to take appropriate precautions to protect their health.
The GHS has called on parents, teachers, traditional authorities, religious leaders, community organisations and local government authorities to intensify public education and promote preventive practices.
It particularly identified the Northern, Upper East, Upper West, Savannah, North East and Bono East regions, alongside other vulnerable areas, as locations where heightened awareness and preparedness would be necessary.
The Service, however, clarified that the anticipated El Niño conditions do not automatically mean Ghana will experience a meningitis outbreak.
It stressed that early preparedness remains essential in view of the expected hot, dry and dusty conditions.
The Ministry of Health and the GHS assured the public that they would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as necessary.
